Which guidelines Review cites

Apple does not always quote guideline numbers in rejection email text, but localization-related holds often map to:

  • Guideline 2.3.8 — Accurate Metadata — App Store product information must accurately represent the app. If your zh-Hans title promises features your description omits, or screenshots show English UI while copy claims full Chinese support, Review treats that as inaccurate metadata for the China storefront.
  • Guideline 4.2.3 — Minimum Functionality / Sufficient Experience — Apps available in a market should offer a complete experience for that market. A zh-Hans row that is blank, placeholder English, or obvious machine translation reads as insufficient localization — especially when China is checked under Pricing and Availability.

These are orientation labels, not legal interpretations. Read Apple's current App Store Review Guidelines and your exact Resolution Center note before you resubmit.

Common rejection patterns we see from indie teams

  • Empty zh-Hans row with China enabled — Connect shows Chinese (Simplified) in the sidebar but name, subtitle, or description were never saved; Review sees English fallback on the China product page
  • Machine translation without edit — literal en-US → zh-Hans paste with 翻译腔, wrong feature names, or keyword stuffing that overflows Connect character caps (see Chinese character limits)
  • Metadata mismatch — Chinese subtitle says "offline mode" but the app requires network; or English What's New describes v2.0 features absent from zh-Hans release notes
  • Screenshot gallery still English — text fields saved in zh-Hans but screenshot slots per device size still show en-US art or English overlay captions on the China storefront
  • IAP or paywall copy skipped — listing localized but in-app purchase display names in Connect remain English-only; Review exercises the paywall on a China-region build
  • Partial resubmit — you fixed the description but not subtitle, keywords, promo text, or What's New — Review reopens the same note on the next pass

Decode your Review note — what to fix first

Open Resolution Center and copy the exact sentence. Match it to the fix column — order matters when you are racing a resubmit window.

"Localization appears incomplete" or "not sufficiently localized"

Treat the entire zh-Hans row as incomplete until every buyer-visible field has saved Chinese text: name, subtitle, description, promotional text, and What's New for the version under review. Add zh-Hans screenshot sets for each required device size — not only the iPhone 6.7" slot.

"Metadata does not match the app" or "misleading metadata"

Line up three sources: your en-US listing, your zh-Hans listing, and what Review sees on device. Remove claims present in only one language. If the app UI is English-only inside, say so honestly in zh-Hans description — do not imply full in-app Chinese if strings were not localized.

"Screenshots do not reflect the localized version"

Upload zh-Hans screenshot galleries or overlays that match the Chinese copy. English UI captures are acceptable only when copy accurately describes that limitation. Mixed galleries (Chinese title + English screenshot captions) often trigger a second hold.

"Promotional text / description not in the language of the storefront"

Scan every text field in the zh-Hans dropdown — promo text and What's New are easy to miss because they sit below the fold in Connect. A filled description with empty promo text still looks English-only on the live page header area.

Resubmit checklist before you click Submit again

  1. Resolution Center — reply with what you changed (field names, not vague "fixed localization")
  2. zh-Hans core fields — name, subtitle, keywords, description saved and within character limits
  3. Version-scoped fields — promotional text and What's New for the build under review
  4. Screenshots per localization — each device size under zh-Hans, not only en-US
  5. IAP display names — if your app monetizes, open Features → In-App Purchases → zh-Hans names
  6. Spot-check on device — China storefront account, compare product page to Connect; mismatch means Review will too
  7. Meaning parity — en-US and zh-Hans describe the same product; no extra promises in one language

FAQ

Why did App Review reject my app for incomplete Chinese localization?

If you enabled the China storefront or added a zh-Hans localization row, Apple expects that row to be complete and accurate — not empty, not obvious machine translation, and not contradicting your en-US listing or in-app experience. Review often cites Guideline 2.3.8 (metadata accuracy) or 4.2.3 (minimum functionality and sufficient localization) when title, subtitle, description, screenshots, or What's New still read as English-only or mismatched on the China product page.

What App Store Review notes mention localization problems?

Common themes include: metadata does not match the app experience in the selected locale; localization appears incomplete; screenshots do not reflect the localized version; promotional text or description is not in the language of the storefront; or the app is not sufficiently localized for markets where it is available. The exact wording varies — treat the note as a checklist, not a single field to patch.

Is machine-translated zh-Hans enough to pass App Review?

Often no. Reviewers compare your Connect fields to what buyers see on device. Raw Google Translate or ChatGPT paste frequently fails on meaning drift, character-limit overflow, keyword stuffing, or screenshot galleries that still show English UI. You need aligned, human-readable zh-Hans fields — not a literal word swap.

What should I fix before resubmitting after a localization rejection?

Audit the zh-Hans row end to end: name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, What's New, screenshot sets per device size, App Preview captions, and IAP display names if your paywall appears in review. Confirm each field matches what the app actually does in Chinese. Submit a metadata-only version if the binary is unchanged, or a new build if in-app strings were part of the note.
